description: Switch the simulated glasses DEVICE MODEL. Meta: rayban_meta, oakley_meta_hstn, oakley_meta_vanguard, rayban_meta_optics, meta_glasses (camera + audio, NO display) and rayban_display (display + Neural Band). The EXPERIMENTAL Android XR pair: android_xr_audio_glasses (camera + audio, no display) and android_xr_display_glasses (adds a display, driven by the temple touchpad, panel 450x394 rather than Meta's 600x600 square). PREVIEW Brilliant Labs: brilliant_halo (256x256 ROUND panel, button + tap) and brilliant_frame (640x400 display and NO SPEAKER — the one device where audio.speak has nowhere to go). PREVIEW HTC: vive_eagle (12 MP camera, four-mic array, open-ear speakers, no display). The selected device's capability profile drives `glasses.display.isAvailable` on the connected app, so this is how an agent tests BOTH branches of a capability-gated feature headless: set `rayban_display` to exercise the display path (glasses.display.show renders), set any no-display model to verify the graceful degradation (the app's isAvailable guard declines; show() no-ops). The model identity ALSO surfaces to the app as `glasses.device.type` (and in the assistant's glasses-state context), so per-model polish — e.g. an Oakley-specific default voice — is testable by switching between models that share the same capability profile. Mirrors the sim's device dropdown — the change persists on the session AND is pushed live to a connected app (the gate flips without a reconnect), and a `device_changed` event lands in getEventLog(filter:'lifecycle'). USE before driving a display flow to pin which device you're testing; pair with getDisplayState / injectInput. DON'T USE for the camera scene (setSimVideo) or voice (injectTranscript).

device.description: The device model to simulate. Display-capable: 'rayban_display' (Meta, Neural Band, 600x600 panel) and 'android_xr_display_glasses' (Android XR, temple touchpad, 450x394 panel) — on both, glasses.display.isAvailable → true and display trees render. The Meta no-display models — 'rayban_meta' (Gen 1/2), 'oakley_meta_hstn', 'oakley_meta_vanguard', 'rayban_meta_optics' (prescription-first Gen 2), 'meta_glasses' (the 2026 Meta-branded line) — share the camera+audio profile but carry distinct identities (glasses.device.type). The two android_xr models switch the session's VENDOR, which is how you check the same code path under a second vendor — but ONLY on an Android session: switching an iOS session onto an android_xr device is REFUSED (vendor_platform_unsupported), because a projected activity is an Android activity and no iOS transport can exist. The brilliant models switch vendor on either platform, as does 'vive_eagle' (HTC VIVE Eagle — camera + four-mic array + open-ear speakers and NO display, the same capability shape as a Ray-Ban Meta from a different vendor, which makes it the cheapest check that your capability branching is genuinely vendor-agnostic). A new session defaults to its vendor's default model (rayban_meta for meta).
